body.statement: If \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\notin\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\), then there exist \(\theta^+,\theta^-\in\Theta_S\) with rational coordinates, \(\theta_j^+(r_j)>0\) and \(\theta_j^-(r_j)>0\) for every \(j\) and every \(r_j\in T_j(S)\), such that \(P_{\theta^+}=P_{\theta^-}\) and \(\tau_{x,y}(\theta^+)\ne\tau_{x,y}(\theta^-)\). The pair may be chosen to differ in exactly one district law.
body.justification: The converse must preserve independence, strict positivity on the active chart, exact support, and exact equality of the observational law.
body.gap: Classical hedges need not preserve a prescribed zero pattern, while polynomial and credal optimization need not emit exact symbolic interior twins.
body.consumer: Every failure certificate becomes a reproducible pair of finite SCMs rather than an optimizer's nonsingleton interval.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(E_j=\mathbb Q^{T_j(S)}\) and \(L_j=\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B_j)\subseteq E_j\).  Choose a basis of each \(L_j\) and extend it to a basis of \(E_j\).  The resulting tensor-product basis shows directly that
\[
\bigcap_{j=1}^m
\left(E_1\otimes\cdots\otimes E_{j-1}\otimes L_j
\otimes E_{j+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes E_m\right)
=\bigotimes_{j=1}^m L_j.                                       \tag{16}
\]
Indeed, membership in the \(j\)-th space on the left forbids every tensor-basis coordinate whose \(j\)-th factor is outside \(L_j\); membership for all \(j\) leaves exactly the coordinates with every factor in its corresponding \(L_j\).

The rows of a Kronecker product are the tensor products of rows of its factors, so
\[
\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^m L_j.      \tag{17}
\]
If \(h=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\) is outside this space, (16) supplies an index \(j\) for which
\[
h\notin E_1\otimes\cdots\otimes E_{j-1}\otimes L_j
\otimes E_{j+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes E_m.                     \tag{18}
\]
Under the standard coordinate pairing, the annihilator of \(L_j\) is \(\ker(B_j)\).  Hence (18) yields a rational vector \(v\in\ker(B_j)\) such that the contraction
\[
g(r_{-j})=\sum_{r_j\in T_j(S)}h(r_j,r_{-j})v(r_j)              \tag{19}
\]
is not the zero tensor on \(\prod_{k\ne j}T_k(S)\).  The row \(B_j[0,\cdot]\) is the all-ones row, and therefore
\[
\sum_{r_j\in T_j(S)}v(r_j)=0.                                 \tag{20}
\]

For each \(k\ne j\), let \(u_k\) be the uniform probability vector on \(T_k(S)\), and, for \(a\in T_k(S)\), set
\[
\eta_{k,a}=\frac{u_k+e_a}{2}.
\]
These are strictly positive rational probability vectors.  They span \(E_k\), because the matrix having them as columns is
\[
\frac12(I+u_k\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}),
\]
whose determinant is \(2^{-|T_k(S)|}(1+\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}u_k)=2^{1-|T_k(S)|}\ne0\).  Consequently, the pure products \(\bigotimes_{k\ne j}\eta_{k,a_k}\) span \(\bigotimes_{k\ne j}E_k\).  Since \(g\ne0\), there is a selection of indices \((a_k:k\ne j)\) for which
\[
c=\sum_{r_{-j}}g(r_{-j})\prod_{k\ne j}\eta_{k,a_k}(r_k)\ne0. \tag{21}
\]
For \(m=1\), the empty product is one and (21) is simply the nonzero scalar contraction furnished by (19).

Let \(u_j\) be uniform on \(T_j(S)\).  Because \(v\) is rational and \(T_j(S)\) is finite, one can choose a rational \(\delta>0\) satisfying
\[
\delta |v(r_j)|<u_j(r_j)
\quad\text{whenever }v(r_j)\ne0.                               \tag{22}
\]
Define
\[
\theta_j^+=u_j+\delta v,\qquad \theta_j^-=u_j-\delta v,
\qquad
\theta_k^+=\theta_k^-=\eta_{k,a_k}\quad(k\ne j),              \tag{23}
\]
and extend all these vectors by zero off their respective \(T_k(S)\).  Equation (20) makes the two vectors in district \(j\) normalized, and (22) makes every coordinate in (23) strictly positive.  All coordinates are rational.  Moreover,
\[
B_j\theta_j^+-B_j\theta_j^-=2\delta B_jv=0,                   \tag{24}
\]
and the signatures in every other district agree because the laws there are identical.  The maximal-support theorem puts both product laws in \(\Theta_S\), and district-signature recovery together with (24) gives
\[
P_{\theta^+}=P_{\theta^-}.                                    \tag{25}
\]
Finally, (19)--(23) give
\[
\tau_{x,y}(\theta^+)-\tau_{x,y}(\theta^-)=2\delta c\ne0.     \tag{26}
\]
Only the \(j\)-th district law differs, which proves every assertion.
